- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes in recent history, often overshooting by 5–15% in the first 5–10 days.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 3–7 days, particularly in downward trends — forecasts are too low and take time to catch up.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias: if recent 7-day average is above 75, model often overpredicts; if below 70, underpredicts.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike in response to minor price changes, then collapse, missing medium-term trends.
- Underestimates price persistence in low-volatility periods — fails to recognize that prices often stay near recent mean for 10+ days.
- When true outcome is above 80, model often overpredicts by 3–8% in the first 5 days, then corrects.
- When true outcome is below 70, model underpredicts by 2–6%, and often fails to recognize the risk of further decline.
- Forecasts are more accurate when recent 30-day mean is stable (±2% over 7 days) — model performs worse when volatility is high or direction is unclear.
